blogs.title: From Black Box to Feature Engineer: How FeatLLM Reimagines LLMs for Tabular AI
blogs.description: Explains the core idea of FeatLLM: using LLMs not to predict directly, but to generate human-readable rules that become features for a lightweight downstream model. Covers why this decoupling slashes inference cost, removes the need for fine-tuning, and sidesteps prompt-length limits.

blogs.title: Why Current LLM-Tabular Methods Struggle—and How FeatLLM Fixes It
blogs.description: Breaks down the pain points of existing approaches (per-sample LLM calls, fine-tuning requirements, context window limits) and shows how FeatLLM’s rule-generation and API-only workflow overcomes them for real-world use.

blogs.title: Prompting for Power: The Two-Step Reasoning Recipe Behind FeatLLM’s Rules
blogs.description: Walks through FeatLLM’s prompt design: Step 1 (general knowledge reasoning about feature–label relations) and Step 2 (rule extraction with few-shot examples). Explains why this structure filters spurious patterns and yields higher-quality, type-consistent rules.

blogs.title: From Text to Toggles: Turning LLM Rules into Binary Features and Predictions
blogs.description: Details how natural-language rules are parsed into executable code to create binary features, then fed into a simple non-negative linear model to compute class likelihoods. Clarifies why learning per-rule weights matters in few-shot settings.

blogs.title: Beating the Context Window: Bagging and Ensembling for Scalable Few-Shot Tables
blogs.description: Describes FeatLLM’s ensemble strategy: randomizing demonstrations, bagging features/instances, and using higher-temperature sampling to diversify rule sets. Shows how this not only boosts robustness but also mitigates prompt-size constraints.

blogs.title: Show Me the Numbers: FeatLLM’s Performance and Cost vs. Popular Baselines
blogs.description: Summarizes results across 13 datasets, highlighting average 10% gains over TabLLM/STUNT and competitive AUROC in ultra-low-shot settings. Compares training and inference time with in-context, TABLET, TabPFN, and classic ML, emphasizing the low inference overhead.

blogs.title: Trust the Rules: Interpretability, Spurious Correlations, and Rule Quality
blogs.description: Explores how FeatLLM’s rule-based features provide interpretable signals, how weight tuning filters weak rules, and why the approach resists spurious columns better than baselines. Includes insights from the AUROC-of-features analysis.

blogs.title: Getting Started with FeatLLM: Practical Tips, Edge Cases, and Extensions
blogs.description: Offers a practitioner’s guide: curating feature descriptions, crafting task statements, choosing rule counts and ensemble size, handling many columns with bagging, and integrating FeatLLM with existing ML stacks. Outlines future directions like richer feature types and large-sample regimes.
